LEDE: One interview for the __ROLE__ role — from “hello” to “we'll get back to you”. The page runs it in order: it asks a question out loud and waits for your answer. Answer some of them yourself, press a GhostMeet chord for others — that is what all of this was built to test.
HINT:
Before you start. Choose this browser as the source of the Them channel in GhostMeet's settings and turn listening on. Do the first run without headphones — that is the worst case, and it is the one worth testing.

How to go through it. Press “Start the interview”: the page plays the opening and the first question, then waits. Answer out loud yourself, or press ⌥⌘A / ⌥⌘Z and read the suggestion. Once you have answered, press “Next”. The badge on a question is a hint, not a rule: where I expect you to answer on your own, where it is worth asking for a brief answer, and where for a detailed one.

The “prepared” badge marks a question whose answer must come from the “Interview context” in the settings. If an invented salary range or somebody else's story arrives instead, that is a defect — write it down verbatim.

Pauses here are never longer than a second — shorter than the threshold at which GhostMeet closes a turn (1.5 s), so the question arrives as one recording. To test the opposite case, push the “Pauses” slider to 2× and the gaps become longer than the threshold; the ones marked red are exactly those.

Do not hide this tab — in a hidden tab the browser coarsens timers to a second and the pauses drift. If the speech comes out of somewhere other than the browser, switch the Them channel to Core Audio Process Tap.
SETUP_TITLE: What to put in the settings before the run
question: question
thanks: Thank you — now write down what did not add up.
noVoices: No English voices found in the system; the list shows everything else. To add one: System Settings → Accessibility → Spoken Content → System Voice → Manage Voices.
oneVoice: There is only one English voice in the system — the second interviewer is told apart by pitch.
